original_question: For each real s>0, does there exist an integer m>=1 such that the entire function sum_{k>=0} k^s x^k/(k!)^m belongs to L-P+, the Laguerre-Polya class of real entire functions with nonnegative Taylor coefficients?
target_in_paper: The draft is trying to capture the Section 3.1 conjecture on the sequence {√k/k!}_{k=0}^∞: the paper explicitly states, “We conjecture that the function φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ (√k/k!)(x^k/k!) belongs to L-P+.” The introduction also identifies this exact function as the main object of Section 3 and notes later supporting results for the same conjectural target. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly asks about an entire function built from coefficients k^s with extra factorial damping and asks whether it lies in L-P+, which is the right zero-distribution framework for the paper’s generalized Bessel-type functions and multiplier-sequence viewpoint. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper does not ask a universal question for every real s>0; it isolates the single nonintegral exponent s=1/2 and suggests that this case is special among sequences of the form {k^s/k!}. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

The denominator power is not existentially quantified: the conjectured function is exactly φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ √k x^k/(k!)^2, so the relevant choice is the fixed value m=2. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

The paper phrases the issue as membership of one specific real entire function in L-P+, not as the existence of some integer m making a broader family work. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

A stand-alone formulation should say that x is the variable of a real entire function (equivalently, a one-variable entire function with real nonnegative Taylor coefficients), not merely a formal series parameter. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

The nearby context is the generalized Bessel-type family B_{s,a}(z)=∑_{n=0}^∞ (n+a)^s z^n/(n!n!), introduced after Theorem 1 and Problem 1; the conjecture is a special case of that setup, not an unrelated existence problem over arbitrary m. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

The k=0 term is included and equals 0, since the conjectured function is written from k=0 onward with coefficient √k/(k!)^2. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

The paper gives an explicitly equivalent multiplier-sequence reformulation via the Pólya–Schur characterization (Theorem 2(iii)); your draft does not note that equivalence. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

The paper’s evidence is asymmetric in s: Example 3 shows that s=1/20 does not give a multiplier sequence, while the authors report that the Jensen polynomials they tested for s=1/2 all had only real zeros. This supports the narrower s=1/2 question rather than your broader for-all-s version. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Is the real entire function φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ √k x^k/(k!)^2 in L-P+, the Laguerre–Pólya class of real entire functions with nonnegative Taylor coefficients? ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is the sequence {√k/k!}_{k=0}^∞ a classical multiplier sequence? ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
justification: The paper first introduces the generalized Bessel-type functions B_{s,a}(z)=∑_{n=0}^∞ (n+a)^s z^n/(n!n!) after observing from Hardy/Ostrovskii that {(k+a)^s} is generally not a multiplier sequence for nonintegral or negative s, and frames the surrounding motivation through Problem 1. Within that program, Section 3.1 singles out the single case s=1/2 and explicitly conjectures that φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ √k x^k/(k!)^2 belongs to L-P+. The authors further say that, among nonintegral exponents s in sequences {k^s/k!}, the case s=1/2 appears special; Example 3 contrasts this with s=1/20, whose Jensen polynomial test fails. Therefore your draft is substantially broader than the paper’s actual target, because it replaces a specific conjecture at s=1/2 and m=2 by a much stronger existence statement over all s>0 and arbitrary integers m≥1. The only paper-explicit alternate formulation justified nearby is the multiplier-sequence reformulation coming from Theorem 2(iii). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
